newsitem.title: UK: Top Conservative's ex-aide defects to UK Labour.
newsitem.headline: Top Conservative's ex-aide defects to UK Labour.

text.p: In another embarrassment for Prime Minister John Major on the eve of his Conservative party's annual conference, Labour announced on Monday the defection of an ex-agent to former Chief Whip Richard Ryder.

Ted Shelton, twice Conservative leader of Breckland District Council in East Anglia, joined Labour because "like thousands of other ordinary decent Conservatives he has decided enough is enough", Labour social security spokeswoman Harriet Harman said.
Harman announced Shelton's defection in Bournemouth as Conservatives gathered for their four-day conference.

The news comes hard on the heels of the defection of ex-party treasurer Lord McAlpine to the Referendum party of Sir James Goldsmith. But Trade Secretary Ian Lang denied that it all added up to a depressing start to the conference.
"On the contrary, I think that the conference... is going to be a great success," Lang told BBC radio.
